title: SwingAI capture manifest
description: Describes one captured shot: the camera streams recorded for it and the timing of every frame in each. Written by the Rust capture runtime, read by the Python analysis pipeline. All cross-component times are integer nanoseconds since the capture session's monotonic origin; see docs/adr/0001-hybrid-rust-python-runtime.md.

schema_version.description: Contract version. Only the exact supported version is accepted; there is no minor-version compatibility yet, so writer and reader move together.

shot_id.description: Stable identifier for this shot. Shared with the analysis result. Must be usable as a directory name.

created_at.description: Wall-clock time the manifest was written. For humans and filing only — never for correlating streams.

trigger_timestamp_ns.description: Capture-session-clock instant the shot trigger fired (e.g. the microphone detecting impact). Absent for a capture that was not triggered.

streams.description: One entry per camera. Camera ids must be unique within a manifest.

schemaVersion.description: The only version this contract revision defines. A later ADR may introduce minor-version compatibility; until then a mismatch is an error rather than a partial read.

rfc3339DateTime.description: An RFC 3339 date-time, e.g. "2026-07-31T14:22:05.412Z" or "2026-07-31T16:22:05.412+02:00". An offset is required. The pattern is present as well as "format" because most JSON Schema validators treat "format" as an annotation unless a format checker is installed. The pattern is structural only — it cannot reject an impossible calendar date such as 2026-02-30, which the Rust implementation does.

timestampNs.description: Nanoseconds since the capture session's monotonic origin. The persisted origin is zero, so values are session-relative and are only comparable within one session. Nonnegative because nothing in a session precedes its own origin — a negative value means a clock-domain conversion went wrong upstream. Nanoseconds because a 240fps frame period is 4.17ms, so millisecond integers would quantize frame timing to a quarter of a frame. Raw camera and audio device stamps may use a different epoch or tick frequency and MUST be converted into this clock domain before being written; the raw values may be kept in a stream's "metadata" but must never appear as a *_timestamp_ns.

relativePath.description: Forward-slash path relative to the directory containing this manifest, e.g. "streams/down_the_line.mkv". Host-independent: backslashes are rejected outright on every platform, which also rules out C:\..., UNC \\server\share, extended-length \\?\C:\..., and rooted \... spellings. Must not be absolute, must not name a drive, and must not escape the directory with "..".

cameraView.description: Note this differs from the Python side's "dtl" (utils/swing_pairing.py, data/annotations.json). The bridge maps; this contract does not accept the abbreviation.

pixelFormat.description: Pixel format of the stored frames. Open set so a vendor format does not require a contract revision. Known values: mono8, mono16, bayer_rg8, bayer_bg8, bgr8, rgb8, yuv420p, nv12.

media.description: Where the frames live, relative to the manifest. Either a single video file or a directory of numbered images.

pattern.description: printf-style filename pattern within the directory, e.g. "frame_%06d.png".

sequenceGap.description: A run of frames the camera reported but did not deliver. Capture-session-clock timestamps bound the hole; the frame index is a stream-local hint only.

start_timestamp_ns.description: Timestamp of the last frame delivered before the gap.

end_timestamp_ns.description: Timestamp of the first frame delivered after the gap. Must be >= start_timestamp_ns.

after_frame_index.description: Index within this stream of the last frame before the gap. Convenience for stream-local seeking; not a cross-component time reference.

camera_id.description: Stable logical identifier for the camera, chosen by the operator (e.g. "fox-dtl"). Unique within a manifest.

serial_number.description: Hardware serial as reported by the camera, when available.

frame_count.description: Number of frames actually stored. Excludes dropped frames.

nominal_fps.description: Rate the camera was configured for. The true rate is (frame_count - 1) / (last - first); they will differ.

last_timestamp_ns.description: Must be >= first_timestamp_ns, and strictly greater when frame_count > 1.

dropped_frame_count.description: Frames the camera reported but that never reached storage.

gaps.description: Where the dropped frames were, when known.

metadata.description: Camera-specific extras (exposure, gain, vendor fields, and the raw device timestamps the session-clock values were converted from). Opaque to the contract and round-tripped unchanged. This is an extension point: unknown keys inside it survive, unknown keys elsewhere in the document do not.
